summary: Rabbi Tawil introduces the book of Melachim, explaining that it is a historical account of the monarchy from Shlomo Hamelech until the destruction of the Bet HaMikdash. He discusses the frailty of David in his old age and the political maneuvering of Adoniyahu to seize the throne, which prompts Natan Hanavi and Bat Sheva to intervene to ensure Shlomo's succession. The class explores the spiritual implications of David's past sins on his current situation and the importance of proactive leadership.
questions: Who is the author of the book of Melachim?
Why were Shaul and David not included in the book of Melachim?
What is the significance of the story of Avishag the Shunamit?
Why did Natan Hanavi and Bat Sheva coordinate their approach to David?
How do David's past sins affect his leadership in his final years?
